# @stolyarovmn/dsh-client-ui-schedule-tab 0.8.0

Stable release for **DeepSeek Harness `0.2.0-rc.2` only**.

`0.8.0` keeps the native Automation Tasks experience and adds the two direct row actions that were missing from `0.7.0`: open the linked Session and delete the task without taking the long native navigation path.

## Highlights

- **Open linked Session** directly from each task row with DSH's native `QueueOutline` icon.
- **Delete** directly from each task row with DSH's native `TrashOutline` icon.
- Clicking the task row itself still opens the native in-page **TaskDetail** on the right; there is no redundant details button.
- Trash opens the **native delete confirmation on the first click**, even when another task was selected before.
- Native Rules editing, Once/Every/Daily/Weekly/Cron controls, date/time/time-zone controls, Delivery records, mutation handling, focus/Escape behavior and deletion toast are preserved.
- Linked Session navigation works both from the row action and from **Linked session** inside TaskDetail.

## Attention and notifications

The attention layer from `0.7.0` remains:

- numeric Automation Tasks unread badge (`1`…`9+`);
- repeated deliveries of the same recurring task counted through retained `schedule.history`;
- one-time delivery popup with **Open conversation**;
- scheduled Session unread indicator;
- separate task-center and Session acknowledgement state;
- overdue warning state;
- browser-local controls for **Popup notifications**, **New tasks**, and **New deliveries**;
- cross-tab preference synchronization;
- English, Chinese and Russian visible strings.

Notification controls now render only on this package's own Plugin Manager detail page. The shared `plugins.detail.section` contribution guards the current `subject`, so the controls no longer appear on Registry Aggregator or any other bundle/row/item page.

## Native DSH UI and architecture

DSH `0.2.0-rc.2` does not expose an additive task-row actions slot. To add the two row actions without maintaining a visually separate task manager, this release builds from a **pinned snapshot of the shipped `dsh-v0.2.0-rc.2` TaskManagerPage/TaskDetail source** and applies one narrow row-actions patch.

The plugin shadows keyed `main/schedules` at `priority: -100`; DSH's shipped registration remains present at its native priority `0`.

The generated helper bundles the pinned DSH primitives and non-platform dependencies such as `clsx`; runtime external checks allow only Harness platform modules (`react`, `react/jsx-runtime`, `react-dom`, `react-dom/client`).

This architecture is intentionally version-specific and must be regenerated/reviewed when moving to another DSH release. If Harness gains a public additive row-actions slot, the pinned page fork should be removed.

## Fixed since the 0.8 development builds

- replaced the misleading New Chat glyph with native `QueueOutline` for existing linked Sessions;
- removed the redundant quick-details action;
- fixed linked Session navigation to use the root `uiWorkspace` service;
- fixed first-click deletion when the row was not already selected;
- fixed `clsx` leaking into the DSH client module table;
- fixed notification settings leaking into unrelated Plugin Manager detail pages;
- kept the right-side task detail genuinely native instead of a hand-redrawn imitation.

## Compatibility

Requires **`@deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.0-rc.2` exactly**.

The official **Automation tasks** capability must be enabled in Plugins → Official (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-schedule-bundle@0.2.0-rc.2`). If Schedule is absent, this enhancer remains inert through optional `remote.schedule` injection.

Legacy compatibility is intentionally not included:

- DSH `0.1.7.x` → use plugin `0.6.15`.
- DSH `0.1.5.x` → use plugin `0.5.1`.

## Install

```bash
pnpm dlx @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.0-rc.2 plugin --profile web add @stolyarovmn/dsh-client-ui-schedule-tab@0.8.0
```

Existing `0.7.0` browser-local seen state and notification preferences are retained on upgrade.

See `CHANGELOG.md` and `MIGRATION_0.2.md` for the detailed compatibility and architecture record.
